# #78826: Build: Document the hooks generated by the wp-build page templates

- **Source:** WordPress/gutenberg
- **Type:** Pull request
- **Author:** @westonruter
- **Labels:** `[Type] Bug`, `Backport to WP Minor Release`, `[Package] wp-build`
- **Merged:** [`3f54b42`](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/commit/3f54b429284db1d0ee9907a0310dade48e0567e1)
- **Discussion:** [#78826](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/78826) · 3 comments · 0 reactions

## Summary

Documentation-only fix to two build templates in the `@wordpress/build` package (`packages/wp-build/templates/page.php.template` and `page-wp-admin.php.template`). The per-page init action hooks — `{page_slug}_init` and `{page_slug}-wp-admin_init` — previously had only bare `//` line comments and now have proper PHPDoc `/** … */` DocBlocks. Additionally, verbatim copies of WordPress core's DocBlocks for `admin_head`, `admin_head-{$hook_suffix}`, `admin_footer`, and `admin_footer-{$hook_suffix}` are replaced with the canonical `/** This action is documented in … */` reference pattern. There are no runtime behavior changes; generated PHP output under `wp-includes/build/pages/` changes only in comments.

## Impact

**Plugin and extension developers targeting `@wordpress/build`-generated pages (font-library, etc.)**
- No action required. The hooks themselves — `{page_slug}_init`, `{page_slug}-wp-admin_init`, and the proxied core admin hooks — are unchanged; only their surrounding comments differ in the generated files.

**Teams running PHPStan against generated page output**
- The missing-DocBlock and duplicated-DocBlock violations that a new PHPStan rule (being introduced on the WordPress core side) flags will now be resolved after a fresh production build.

**`@wordpress/build` package maintainers / contributors**
- Future hook documentation in these templates should follow the same two patterns enforced here: inline DocBlock for page-specific hooks, `/** This action/filter is documented in <canonical-file> */` for re-fired core hooks.

## Technical details

**`page-wp-admin.php.template` — init action DocBlock**

Before:
```php
// Fire init action for extensions to register routes and menu items
do_action( '{{PAGE_SLUG}}-wp-admin_init' );
```
After:
```php
/**
 * Fires when the {{PAGE_SLUG}} admin page is initialized so extensions can register routes and menu items.
 */
do_action( '{{PAGE_SLUG}}-wp-admin_init' );
```

**`page.php.template` — init action DocBlock**

Same pattern applied to `do_action( '{{PAGE_SLUG}}_init' )`. No `@since` tag is added in either template because one template generates pages introduced across multiple WordPress versions, making any single version tag incorrect.

**`page.php.template` — core hook reference comments (four replacements)**

The full DocBlocks for `admin_head`, `admin_head-{$hook_suffix}`, `admin_footer`, and `admin_footer-{$hook_suffix}` (previously copied verbatim, including `@since 2.1.0` / `@since 1.2.0` / `@since 2.8.0` tags) are removed and replaced:
```php
/** This action is documented in wp-admin/admin-header.php */
do_action( "admin_head-{$hook_suffix}" );

/** This action is documented in wp-admin/admin-header.php */
do_action( 'admin_head' );

/** This action is documented in wp-admin/admin-footer.php */
do_action( 'admin_footer', '' );

/** This action is documented in wp-admin/admin-footer.php */
do_action( "admin_footer-{$hook_suffix}" );
```

The `{page_slug}_boot_dependencies` filter's existing inline DocBlock is unchanged — it is genuinely page-specific and not a re-fire of a core hook, so inline documentation is correct there.

Changes take effect in the generated files under `wp-includes/build/pages/` only after running `npm run build`.

## Contribution

Opened and merged by @westonruter as a follow-up to #73120 and #73137. The two deficiencies — undocumented init actions and duplicated core hook DocBlocks — were surfaced by a PHPStan rule being introduced on the WordPress core side that flags exactly these patterns. @t-hamano reviewed the PR and requested it also be backported to the 7.0.1 minor release (to accompany the correct backport of #75985). The PR was authored with Claude Code (Claude Opus) assistance, with all changes reviewed by @westonruter.
